question.problem:
Which of the following are stochastic matrices?

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0.1 & 0.7 \\ 0.9 & 0.3\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}0.45 & 0.35 \\ 0.25 & 0.65\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a stochastic vector is a vector with nonnegative entries that add up to $1.$ A matrix is stochastic if all its columns are stochastic vectors.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices in turn.

- Matrix $U$ is a stochastic matrix. Indeed, each column is a stochastic vector (the corresponding entries are nonnegative and add up to one): 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}0.1 & 0.7 \\ 0.9 & 0.3\end{aligned}]\,\begin{aligned}0.1+0.9=1 \\ 0.7+0.3=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

- Matrix $V$ is *not* a stochastic matrix since its first column is not a stochastic vector (the corresponding entries don't add up to one): 

$$
[\begin{aligned}0.45 & 0.35 \\ 0.25 & 0.65\end{aligned}]
$$

- Matrix $W$  *not* a stochastic matrix since its second column is not a stochastic vector (it contains negative entries):

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$U$ only."
